When relics arrived in Darnassus from the fallen druid Mulgris Deepriver—who perished fighting the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands—Mathrengyl was deeply moved to discover the investigator was a tauren. Reflecting on the Cenarion Circle's shared mission, he quietly mused that the tauren may not have drifted nearly as far from the teachings of Cenarius as the Archdruid insists.

npc:motega-firemane.text: Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

npc:onyxia.text: Onyxia. Onyxia is the broodmother of the black dragonflight and the devious daughter of Deathwing. From her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she schemes to restore the black dragonflight's dominion over the mortal kingdoms.

npc:orgrim-doomhammer.text: Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces. Escaping human captivity, Doomhammer lived in hiding until he met Thrall, Durotan's orphaned son. Reinvigorated by the young shaman's vision, Orgrim rallied what was left of the orcish clans to storm the internment camps and break their people free. During a fierce battle at an encampment in the Arathi Highlands, the Warchief was struck down from behind by a lance. As he lay dying, he bestowed his black plate armor, his ancestral weapon—the Doomhammer—and the title of Warchief upon Thrall. In his honor, the liberated outpost was renamed Hammerfall, and the newly founded capital in Durotar was christened Orgrimmar.

npc:ozzie-togglevolt.text: Ozzie Togglevolt. Ozzie Togglevolt is a gnome engineer and survivor of Gnomeregan's fall, currently operating out of the snowy village of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Haunted by the tragedy that struck his people, he works alongside his partner Razzle Sprysprocket to research a remedy for the irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt was inside the subterranean wonders of Gnomeregan when catastrophe struck. When the toxic fallout was vented throughout the corridors to stem the trogg invasion, Ozzie stood right beside his fellow gnome, Gnoarn. A sudden radioactive discharge struck Gnoarn directly, altering him forever before Ozzie's eyes. Though Ozzie made it to the surface alive and reached the haven of Dun Morogh, the horrifying memory of that disaster never left him. Now established in Kharanos, Ozzie spends his days tinkering alongside Razzle Sprysprocket. Their primary technological and scientific endeavor remains intensely personal: finding a way to reverse the horrific mutagenic fallout of their lost home and cure the suffering leper gnomes.

npc:pelturas-whitemoon.text: Pelturas Whitemoon. Pelturas Whitemoon is a night elf father dwelling in Astranaar whose young daughter, Relara, has been struck by a terrible, corrupting illness. Desperate to save her, he works closely with local herbalist Orendil Broadleaf and traveling Alliance champions to gather sacred remedies from the surrounding wilds. His quest to heal Relara takes adventurers into some of Ashenvale's oldest sacred groves and ruins. Residing in the serene boughs of Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon lives the quiet life typical of forest-dwelling Kaldorei, often venturing out with his young daughter Relara to collect shimmering moonstones around Fallen Sky Lake. However, when Relara falls critically ill with a mysterious affliction, his quiet world collapses into frantic desperation. Astranaar is besieged on many fronts, but for Pelturas, nothing in the great forest matters more than saving his child.

npc:priestess-alathea.text: Priestess Alathea. Priestess Alathea is a night elf priest trainer residing within the tranquil halls of the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Devoted to the Moon Goddess, she guides novitiates in the sacred arts and racial blessings bestowed by Elune. Her teachings help night elf practitioners attune their minds to defensive prayers and celestial magic. Standing within the soaring silver heights of Darnassus's grandest sanctuary, Priestess Alathea serves the Sisterhood of Elune as an instructor and spiritual guide. As night elf initiates progress beyond the quiet boughs of Shadowglen, they are directed to the Temple of the Moon to deepen their covenant with the Goddess. Alathea stands among the priestesses ready to impart sacred knowledge to those who dedicate their lives to healing, warding, and divine light. Unlike priests of the Holy Light who draw strength strictly from human and dwarven traditions, kaldorei priests draw directly upon the grace of Elune. Alathea plays a key role in testing and granting blessings tailored to night elves, such as Stars of Elune and Elune's Grace. Through her guidance, acolytes learn how to weave starlight into shields of swiftness and defensive power to survive the growing perils facing Kalimdor.

npc:raene-wolfrunner.text: Raene Wolfrunner. Raene Wolfrunner is an accomplished Sentinel officer and hunter stationed at the heart of Astranaar in Ashenvale. Accompanied by her loyal wolf and saber cat companions, she coordinates defense efforts across the forest against encroaching Horde forces and corrupted furbolg tribes. She serves as a vital anchor for Alliance champions striving to protect the sacred wilderness. Raene Wolfrunner stands watchful in Astranaar alongside her trusty saber cat Korra and wolf Dagri. As an officer among the Sentinels, she oversees patrols throughout Ashenvale and coordinates intelligence reaching beyond its borders, dispatching scouts like Kaela Shadowspear into neighboring regions such as the Stonetalon Mountains. Beyond the tensions with the Horde, Raene is deeply invested in addressing the dark taint sickening Ashenvale's native denizens. She directs campaigns against hostile furbolg tribes, including aggressive strikes against the Foulweald camps harassing travelers and targeted culls against rising Thistlefur leadership. Her subordinate scouts keep close watch over changing furbolg behavior, relying on Raene's steady command to protect local settlements and passing wayfarers from coordinated ambushes.

npc:rejold-barleybrew.text: Rejold Barleybrew. Rejold Barleybrew is a master dwarven brewer stationed in the lakeside settlement of Brewnall Village in western Dun Morogh. Devoted to perfecting hearty mountain spirits, he regularly enlists travelers to gather regional ingredients and test his potent recipes across the snowy valley. In Dun Morogh, brewing is treated not merely as trade, but as a defining art form. Rejold Barleybrew embodies this tradition from Brewnall Village, an outpost nestled near the frozen lake of the Iceflow River. Rather than settling for common tavern swill, Rejold continually refines his blends, seeking rare hops, mountain minerals, and pristine ice water to produce stouts capable of warming the stoutest dwarven warriors. Rejold is relentless in his quest for ideal flavor profiles, sending adventurous spirits across Dun Morogh to collect vital components for drinks like Shimmer Stout. Whether trading favors with the siege pilots of Steelgrill's Depot or arranging deliveries to thirsty patrons, his work ensures that the cold, trogg-plagued roads of Dun Morogh remain tolerable with an ample supply of hearty ale.

npc:rethiel-the-greenwarden.text: Rethiel the Greenwarden. Rethiel the Greenwarden is an ancient, sentient bog beast residing in the Green Belt within the Wetlands. Deeply attuned to the natural balance of the marsh, he watches over the land and enlists travelers to cull threats that disrupt its harmony. Standing amidst the damp thickets of the Green Belt, Rethiel is a towering creature of moss, peat, and primal plant life. While many bog beasts in the marshlands wander aimlessly as aggressive predators, Rethiel possesses a rare, conscious awareness and a sorrowful voice. He perceives the wetlands not merely as murky terrain, but as a living ecosystem that currently cries out under the weight of foreign predation and corruption. Rethiel seeks to alleviate the suffering of the Wetlands by dispatching sympathetic adventurers against its major agitators. He urges visitors to hunt down destructive Mosshide gnolls who ravage the wildlife, strip them of the crude flints they use to burn the marsh's living trees, and thin out the diseased fen creepers that fester in the marsh waters. Through these cullings, he hopes to restore peace to the wounded soil.

npc:rorian-the-dayseeker.text: Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian the Dayseeker is an elder Skyborne figure situated in Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. He oversees the initiation of young fledglings as they discover their calling, step into maturity, and attune themselves to the natural elements of their homeland. Under his watchful guidance, newcomers learn the fundamentals of survival, tradition, and service to their community. Within the serene confines of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker stands as one of the primary mentors for the fledgling Skyborne. Revered for his experience and calm wisdom, Rorian directs youth during their crucial transition into adulthood. It is under his instruction that initiates undertake their traditional rite of passage, marking their readiness to defend and support their island home. Beyond fundamental trials, Rorian points promising initiates toward specialized paths suited to their talents. Whether an aspiring warrior, hunter, rogue, mage, shaman, or druid, fledglings are directed by Rorian to dedicated trainers across the isle. He also alerts them to elemental disturbances disrupting the island's harmony, instilling an enduring duty to preserve balance across the windswept heights.

npc:senani-thunderheart.text: Senani Thunderheart. Senani Thunderheart is a tauren huntress stationed at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale, just north of the Barrens. Serving the Horde, she tests the mettle of passing travelers by challenging them to pursue the fierce wild predators that roam the ancient forest. Through her trials, hunters prove their skill while thinning the deadly beasts prowling near Horde territory. Found keeping camp at Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart represents the hunting traditions of the tauren amid the shadowed groves of Ashenvale. Far from the open plains of Mulgore, she directs Horde adventurers to test their tracking and combat prowess against the forest's apex beasts. She views the hunt as both an honorable challenge and a necessary ritual to survive in an untamed, contested land. Senani oversees the traditional hunting trials of Ashenvale, directing hunters toward three notorious predators: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the hippogryph Sharptalon. Claiming their tokens—a paw, a head, and a claw—is a rite of passage that demonstrates a hunter's respect for the land and dominion over its fiercest denizens.

npc:senir-whitebeard.text: Senir Whitebeard. Senir Whitebeard is a dwarven dignitary and field agent stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Serving as a special envoy from the Senate of Ironforge, he is tasked with monitoring the growing threats encircling Dun Morogh. His mission centers on evaluating the Frostmane troll offensive and reporting their movements directly back to the dwarven leadership. While most travelers visit Kharanos for its bustling inn and famous stout, Senir Whitebeard is here on official business. As a representative sent directly by the Senate of Ironforge, his presence highlights how seriously the high halls take the destabilization of Dun Morogh. He serves as an essential bridge between local scouts facing danger on the snowy frontier and the legislators arguing policy behind the city's stone gates. Senir's primary concern is the escalating aggression of the Frostmane trolls. Displaced and desperate in the frozen crags, the trolls have begun pushing dangerously close to dwarven settlements and roads. Rather than charging into battle himself, the venerable envoy gathers reconnaissance on troll positions, particularly around their stronghold, compiling meticulous reports so Ironforge's military commanders can strike decisively.

npc:shael-dryn.text: Shael'dryn. Shael'dryn is an inquisitive dryad residing beside the Moonwell of Purity, east of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. She serves as a vital contact for night elf scouts investigating forest corruption. She plays a pivotal role in aiding Astranaar's sentinels with cleansing relics to combat demonic and foul influences spreading across the wilderness. Stationed beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn keeps watch alongside the night elf sentinels guarding the eastern approaches of the forest. When corruption surfaces among the local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, her deep natural understanding allows her to guide adventurers through the steps required to restore spiritual balance.

npc:sprite-jumpsprocket.text: Sprite Jumpsprocket. Sprite Jumpsprocket is an apprentice gnome engineer currently residing in the busy Dwarven District of Stormwind City. Like many gnomes who sought refuge following the fall of Gnomeregan, she pursues technical craft and innovation alongside her fellow tinkers. Her presence highlights the thriving community of dwarven and gnomish artisans who keep the capital city supplied with gears, gadgets, and mechanical expertise. In the soot-covered streets and bustling workshops of the Dwarven District, gnomes and dwarves work shoulder-to-shoulder forging metal and designing intricate contraptions. Sprite Jumpsprocket serves as an apprentice engineer in this vibrant hub. Having integrated into the kingdom's capital, apprentice tinkers like Sprite hone their craft under experienced masters, contributing their inventive minds to the everyday mechanisms and technological marvels of the Alliance. Following the devastating loss of Gnomeregan, displaced gnomes dispersed across Alliance lands, bringing their singular knack for tinkering, chemistry, and mechanics with them. In Stormwind City, gnomes found a welcoming sanctuary within the Dwarven District, where blast furnaces and workbenches are plentiful. Sprite Jumpsprocket represents this resilient, forward-looking spirit—determined to master the complex discipline of engineering despite the hardships faced by her kin.

npc:sten-stoutarm.text: Sten Stoutarm. Sten Stoutarm is a practical dwarven outfitter and courier stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Responsible for keeping new recruits equipped and managing local dispatches, he helps ensure that novice mountaineers stay warm, fed, and informed despite the harsh mountain conditions. Positioned near the heart of Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm is one of the first friendly faces new dwarven and gnomish recruits encounter outside Anvilmar's tavern. With the valley isolated by winter blizzards and encroaching dangers, Sten takes it upon himself to outfit green apprentices with sturdy gear before they freeze or wander unprepared into the drifts. Beyond assembling winter outfitting from local wolf hides, Sten serves as an informal postmaster for Coldridge Valley. He handles messages passed through the treacherous Coldridge Pass and distributes official runes, memoranda, and orders to class trainers throughout the basin, ensuring novice warriors, priests, and mages get their instructions despite the hostile trogg presence blocking the tunnels.

npc:sven-yorgen.text: Sven Yorgen. Sven Yorgen is a grieving farmer camped on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank in western Duskwood, accompanied by his companion Lars. Having survived the brutal slaughter of his family at the Yorgen Farmstead, Sven is consumed by a relentless drive to uncover who brought ruin upon his home and exact vengeance. Sven was born before the First War, old enough to recall the days before the region became shrouded in gloom following Medivh's fall. For years he worked the soil at the Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood alongside his wife and children. That quiet existence ended in sudden violence when mysterious Dark Riders raided his homestead while he was away, butchering his family and turning the farm into a graveyard. Unable to return to the ruins of his home, Sven established a secluded refuge on the Hushed Bank with his friend Lars. Distrustful of outsiders, he demands proof of loyalty from travelers before sharing his burden. Sven spotted a skulking figure lurking near his devastated farmstead and became convinced this interloper was either directly responsible for the massacre or tied to the sinister horsemen who tore his world apart.

npc:tallonkai-swiftroot.text: Tallonkai Swiftroot. Tallonkai Swiftroot is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Concerned with the emerging corruption tainting the great boughs, he enlists young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and stem the foul forces plaguing the woods. Dwelling in the canopy settlement of Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot keeps a watchful eye over the surrounding woods. Like many night elves living beneath the boughs of the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by the unnatural agitation of the wildlife and the unsettling shadows gathering at the edges of their settlements. Tallonkai directs adventurers to confront foul entities disturbing Teldrassil's peace. His concerns include corrupted dream catchers crafted to protect sleeping druids, vicious gnarlpine furbolgs succumbing to a dark malaise, and the corrupted Gnarlpine mystics led by Ferocitas the Dream Eater. To Tallonkai, cleansing these disturbances is crucial to defending the fragile home of the Kaldorei.

npc:tavernkeep-smitts.text: Tavernkeep Smitts. Tavernkeep Smitts is the barkeep of the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. Operating at the social center of Duskwood, Smitts possesses an encyclopedic knowledge of town gossip and unsolved local tragedies. His long memory and keen eye make him an invaluable contact for anyone investigating the region's dark history. Behind the bar of the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Tavernkeep Smitts offers warm hearth fires and drink to the weary travelers, local townspeople, and nervous Night Watch guards braving Duskwood's perils. As one of the longest-standing public faces in town, Smitts hears every rumor that filters through the gloom. While other townsfolk shrink behind locked shutters, Smitts maintains a pragmatic, observant eye on everyone who passes through his door, noting unusual behavior, hurried departures, and strange patrons.

npc:terenthis.text: Terenthis. Terenthis is a night elf druid stationed in the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Representing the Cenarion Circle, he is investigating the alarming corruption spreading through Darkshore and Teldrassil. He enlists capable travelers to gauge rising threats along the coast and assist local allies trapped by corrupted wildlife. Sent to Auberdine by the Cenarion Circle, Terenthis focuses on tracking the spread of Fel Moss and other corruptive forces seeping into Darkshore from Teldrassil. The night elves view this creeping blight with immense concern, fearing the wild balance of northern Kalimdor may fracture completely if left unchecked. Terenthis works to uncover the root causes of the rot and devise ways to halt its advance before it consumes the forests.

npc:theocritus.text: Theocritus. Archmage Theocritus is an eccentric human wizard who resides at the peak of the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. He lives independently, surrounded by servants and magical scrying devices. From his high sanctum, Theocritus directs his arcane talents toward keeping watch over the kingdom and combating his dark rival, the rogue mage Morganth. Archmage Theocritus keeps an independent stronghold in the kingdom of Stormwind. He settled in the prominent Tower of Azora, situated near the eastern road to Redridge. Theocritus is known for his eccentric habits and comfortable lifestyle, employing an extensive household staff that includes numerous gnomish attendants and his own dedicated clothier, Morley Eberlein. Though he keeps himself largely detached from the mundane concerns of local villagers, his presence serves as a critical magical bulwark in eastern Elwynn. Theocritus's greatest ongoing concern is the fallen mage Morganth, a dangerous warlock operating from the Tower of Ilgalar in the nearby Redridge Mountains. Viewing Morganth both as a personal nemesis and a severe peril to Stormwind, Theocritus has dedicated months of arcane research to undermining him. Through scrying artifacts like the Eye of Azora, Theocritus monitors the villain's actions and delves into his thoughts. He also works to turn Morganth's own creations against him, studying the magical pendants carried by the Shadowhide gnolls in hopes of transmitting an arcane pulse that can immobilize the entire pack.

npc:thyn-tel-bladeweaver.text: Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver is a night elf sentinel stationed at the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She is deeply troubled by the disappearance of Priestess Velinde Starsong and dispatches trusted Alliance adventurers to track down clues regarding her whereabouts. Through her inquiries, she seeks to piece together the unraveling mystery behind the Scythe of Elune. Standing watch over Darnassus from the Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver represents the vigilant military arm of the kaldorei. When Priestess Velinde Starsong mysteriously vanished without leaving word, Thyn'tel refused to let the trail go cold. Sensing that grave forces were involved, she takes it upon herself to commission adventurers willing to dig into the priestess's personal belongings and uncover where her journey led.

npc:tirion-fordring.text: Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the order Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded during the Second War, Tirion fought the Old Horde with plate, hammer, and holy devotion. He was revered as an unyielding paragon of the Holy Light. Following the Second War, Tirion governed the region of Hearthglen from Mardenholde Keep with his wife Karandra and young son Taelan. His reign ended when he encountered an aged orc warrior named Eitrigg living as a hermit. Recognizing the veteran's deep honor, Tirion gave his word to protect him. When Alliance authorities discovered Eitrigg, Tirion fought his own countrymen to uphold his oath. For this treason against the Alliance of Lordaeron, Tirion was stripped of his nobility, excommunicated by the Silver Hand, and banished into exile; Uther spared his wife and son from the sentence.

npc:tiza-battleforge.text: Tiza Battleforge. Tiza Battleforge is a veteran dwarven paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. Renowned for her steadfast devotion and insight, she guides young dwarven paladins along the path of virtue, charity, and self-sacrifice. Through study of the sacred texts and trials in the field, she tests whether initiates are truly ready to wield the Light's gift of resurrection. Within the serene chambers of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge stands as one of the most respected dwarven paladins of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Initiates across the Alliance—directed by tutors such as Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, Azar Stronghammer in Dun Morogh, and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind—are sent to her to advance their spiritual education. Tiza believes that the Holy Light demands more than martial skill; it requires humble service, compassion, and unwavering fortitude against the encroaching darkness of the Scourge and other threats.

npc:verner-osgood.text: Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense. Verner's troubles extend far beyond a shortage of iron. The gnolls infesting the Redridge hills routinely ambush livestock, carrying off working horses whenever they stray outside the town perimeter. Driven to exasperation by the destruction of his livelihood, Verner actively recruits traveling adventurers to cull the marauding packs and hunt down their ferocious packleader, Yowler.

npc:viktori-prism-antras.text: Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet. Constructing such a delicate apparatus is no simple matter in a cursed forest. Viktori works from blueprints provided by his gnomish friend, Cog Glitzspinner. To complete the device, he enlists passersby to track down rare lens-crafting materials and mechanical housings, ranging from finely cut glass to metal lenses scattered across perilous territory.

npc:warden-thelwater.text: Warden Thelwater. Warden Thelwater is the besieged overseer of the Stockade, Stormwind City's underground maximum-security prison. Caught unprepared when a violent riot erupted among the Defias prisoners, he now desperately recruits capable adventurers to quell the rebellion before word spreads to the city above. Hidden beneath the canals of Stormwind, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them securely locked away, but an organized revolt took the guards completely off guard. With the prisoners overwhelming security and taking control of the cells, Thelwater found himself barricaded at the threshold, struggling to contain an armed insurrection right beneath the streets of the capital.

npc:william-pestle.text: William Pestle. William Pestle is a human alchemist staying inside Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Together with his brother Morgan, he helps run the apothecary shop in Stormwind's Trade District. He frequently employs traveling adventurers to gather odd reagents like kobold candles, murloc kelp, and herbal supplies. While his brother Morgan Pestle manages the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City, William operates out of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Being stationed in Elwynn Forest allows him to work closely with local gatherers and secure raw materials that city shops constantly require. He maintains regular shipments back to the capital, ensuring Stormwind's citizens have steady access to restorative salves, draughts, and powders. William's craft often demands unusual components that go beyond simple garden herbs. He frequently commissions newcomers to gather wax candles carried by Elwynn's infesting kobolds, as well as crystal kelp taken from the murlocs of Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Although such concoctions seem bizarre to the uninitiated, William insists these strange ingredients possess potent alchemical virtues.

npc:wizbang-cranktoggle.text: Wizbang Cranktoggle. Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnome engineer residing on the upper floor of the Auberdine inn. Despite being far from the cog-filled halls of Gnomeregan or Ironforge, he has turned his mechanical ingenuity toward setting up and maintaining automated communication devices known as buzzboxes across the wild coast of Darkshore. While the night elves of Auberdine prefer living in harmony with nature and leaning upon ancient customs, Wizbang Cranktoggle represents the curious, tinkering presence of the Alliance. Perched on the top floor of Auberdine's inn, surrounded by tools and spare components, Wizbang pays little mind to the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor, focusing instead on pragmatic mechanical challenges. Wizbang's primary project along Darkshore is deploying and maintaining his peculiar invention: the buzzbox. Designed to establish automated reporting and long-distance communication across the rugged, sprawling coastline, these contraptions often suffer from coastal weathering and the hostility of local wildlife. Wizbang frequently recruits travelers to gather components, salvage tools like gaffer jacks, and recover electropellers to keep his mechanical surveillance functioning.

subzone:addle-s-stead.text: Addle's Stead. Addle's Stead is an abandoned farmstead in southwestern Duskwood, lying quiet under the forest's gloom south of Raven Hill. While its original homesteaders fled long ago, the farm has become a hidden staging ground for the Defias Brotherhood. Like many of the forgotten homesteads scattered across Duskwood, Addle's Stead fell into disrepair when darkness and ruin enveloped the region. Rather than remaining empty, the farm has been repurposed by the Defias Brotherhood. Agents prowl the perimeter, lurk within the decrepit farmhouse, and stash supplies in the barn, using the shadowy cover of southwestern Duskwood to escape the notice of both the Night Watch and Stormwind authorities.

subzone:aldrassil.text: Aldrassil. Aldrassil is the colossal bough-tree and settlement nestled at the heart of Shadowglen in northeastern Teldrassil. Serving as the primary refuge and training ground for young kaldorei, its carved hollows shelter trainers, merchants, and local leadership. Rising high above the secluded vale of Shadowglen, Aldrassil functions as both shelter and civic hub for young night elves taking their first steps in the world. Built into and around the colossal trunk of this ancient growth, winding ramps lead past class trainers and artisans to the high roost where Tenaron Stormgrip oversees the glade's protection. While the world bough Teldrassil stretches across the horizon, Aldrassil provides a safe, grounded canopy where novices learn their arts before venturing down into the troubled wilds of Kalimdor.

subzone:alexston-farmstead.text: Alexston Farmstead. The Alexston Farmstead is a derelict farm in Westfall, overgrown and prowled by haywire Harvest Watchers. Once the childhood home of Stormwind's city architect, Baros Alexston, it has fallen into ruin like much of the breadbasket around it. Situated amidst the dry plains of Westfall, the Alexston Farmstead stands as another grim testament to the kingdom's neglect. Like neighboring estates, the farm was abandoned by its caretakers when banditry erupted across the countryside. Today, the fields are overgrown, and the mechanical Harvest Watchers left behind to tend the crops have spun out of control, violently attacking anyone who approaches the barren farmhouse. Despite its bleak state, the farm is tied to one of Stormwind's most prominent citizens. Baros Alexston, the skilled architect who helped design parts of the rebuilt capital, spent his youth toiling on these very fields. He left the farmstead long before the unrest began to pursue his trade in masonry and construction, leaving behind a memento of his early life nestled among the ruins.

subzone:algaz-station.text: Algaz Station. Algaz Station is a dwarven military outpost situated in northwestern Loch Modan, directly south of the fortified pass of Dun Algaz. Manning the approach to the northern tunnels, its garrison of Mountaineers helps safeguard travelers and watch the frontier leading toward the Wetlands. Perched just east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, Algaz Station serves as a vital strategic watchpoint for the kingdom of Ironforge. A cadre of dwarven Mountaineers maintains a permanent vigil here, keeping the vital road between Loch Modan and the northern lowlands open to trade and troop movements. Given the frequent threats in the surrounding hills, from wandering beasts to encroaching troggs, the outpost provides respite, repairs, and martial support for weary travelers before they venture through the mountain tunnels.

subzone:alterac-mountains.text: Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes. Following the devastation of the Third War, the mountains collapsed into complete lawlessness. The disinherited nobles of the realm banded together to form the Syndicate, operating out of the ruins of Strahnbrad and plotting to reclaim their lost dominion through sabotage and assassination. Between ruthless Crushridge ogres occupying the shattered capital, marauding gnolls, and the shattered magical ruins around Dalaran, the passes of Alterac remain some of the most perilous pathways in Lordaeron.

subzone:alther-s-mill.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a ruined lumber mill tucked into the rugged hills northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital source of processed timber for local builders, the abandoned grounds have deteriorated into a haven for feral scavengers and prowling predators. For adventurers traveling east toward Stonewatch, the dilapidated structures serve as a grim landmark marking the boundary of safe frontier territory. Before the region fell prey to invading predators and orc raids, Alther's Mill bustled with timber trade that supplied the construction of Lakeshire and surrounding settlements. Its quiet clearing northeast of Lake Everstill provided ready access to mountain timber stands. As turmoil mounted across the kingdom of Stormwind and the Blackrock clan pushed down from the heights of Stonewatch, local millers abandoned the facility, leaving the dry timber buildings and wheel to decay into rot. In the absence of human workers, the mill became infested with monstrous tarantulas, carrion vultures, and opportunistic raiders. Travelers cutting through the path to the eastern passes must skirt its shadowed perimeter carefully. In recent years, shadowy operatives and thieves have also taken advantage of the abandoned compound, using its discarded storage boxes and hidden corners to hone illicit lockpicking crafts and covert trades far from the eyes of the Lakeshire Town Watch.

subzone:amberstill-ranch.text: Amberstill Ranch. Amberstill Ranch is a tranquil dwarven homestead nestled along the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, directly north of Gol'Bolar Quarry. It serves as the primary breeding and training grounds for Ironforge's celebrated mountain rams. Adventurers visit the ranch to acquire hardy dwarven mounts, train in riding, or help the family defend their livestock from local predators. Tucked against the crags of Dun Morogh, Amberstill Ranch is renowned throughout Khaz Modan for raising the sturdiest mountain rams in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Amberstill family manages the stables and paddocks, training these sure-footed beasts to navigate treacherous snowy passes and steep alpine cliffs. Outside of supplying riding mounts and domestic livestock, the family often contends with the savage fauna of the hills, particularly wandering wendigos drawn by the scent of fresh flock.

subzone:ameth-aran.text: Ameth'Aran. Ameth'Aran is an ancient ruin in southern Darkshore, once a thriving city where Queen Azshara's Highborne practiced arcane sorcery. When the Great Sundering shattered the ancient world, the city fell with it. Today, its broken colonnades are haunted by the vengeful ghosts of the elves who died there. Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and its sister settlement, Bashal'Aran, stood as twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Under the favor of Queen Azshara, its ruling nobility dedicated themselves to unrestrained arcane experimentation. Governed from afar by the sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in the Tower of Althalaxx, the city thrived until the catastrophic collapse of the Well of Eternity tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

subzone:angerfang-encampment.text: Angerfang Encampment. The Angerfang Encampment is the primary stronghold of the Dragonmaw clan in the central Wetlands. Led by Chieftain Nek'rosh Skullcrusher, these renegade orcs use the sprawling camp as a staging ground to threaten nearby dwarven settlements and plot the destruction of Menethil Harbor. Sprawling across the muck of the central Wetlands, the Angerfang Encampment serves as the fortified heart of Dragonmaw power in the region. Unlike the scattered raiding parties found wandering the marshes, this compound boasts heavily defended barricades, watchtowers, and a formidable host of warriors, bonewarders, and dark spellcasters loyal to the old ways. From here, the Dragonmaw project military force across the marshlands, raiding travelers along the roads and menacing nearby dwarven digs like Whelgar's Excavation Site.

subzone:anvilmar.text: Anvilmar. Anvilmar is a fortified dwarven outpost nestled in the snowy depths of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. Centered around a massive stone forge, it serves as the primary training grounds and rallying point for young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomish refugees beginning their adventures. Tucked away in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley, Anvilmar stands as an enduring symbol of dwarven perseverance. Dominated by a roaring central forge, this sturdy masonry complex houses class mentors, supply vendors, and veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before sending them out into the wider kingdom. Though sheltered behind towering drifts, the settlement remains on constant guard against the hostile Frostmane trolls and aggressive wild beasts prowling the frozen valley. The settlement likely takes its proud name from High King Modimus Anvilmar, the ancient sovereign who ruled all dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. Today, the garrison remains vigilant, ensuring the forge fires stay lit against the trolls and beasts of the valley.

subzone:astranaar.text: Astranaar. Astranaar is the primary Night Elf settlement in central Ashenvale, built across a serene lake island straddling the ancient forest road. Serving as the beating heart of Alliance operations in the region, it provides vital refuge to travelers facing encroaching threats from hostile furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde. Situated atop an island in the middle of a forest lake, Astranaar stands as the largest night elven settlement in Ashenvale. Connected to the mainland by wooden footbridges spanning the waters, the town houses sentinels, priests, and artisans who keep vigil over the woodlands. In addition to offering basic comforts such as an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker, its elevated perches host a flight master providing hippogryph travel to distant outposts across Kalimdor. Despite its tranquil waters and glowing lanterns, Astranaar exists in a state of perpetual readiness. Local leaders like Raene Wolfrunner coordinate patrols and defensive actions against the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs encroaching from the north, fearful they may mount a direct assault on the settlement.

subzone:auberdine.text: Auberdine. Auberdine is a coastal night elven port town on the gloomy shores of Darkshore, serving as the Alliance's primary maritime gateway to northern Kalimdor. Sheltered beneath overcast skies and pine-covered bluffs, it connects the island home of Teldrassil to the Eastern Kingdoms while serving as an administrative haven against the encroaching wilderness. Resting along the shores of the Veiled Sea, Auberdine is the only major settlement to successfully endure in modern Darkshore. Unlike the secluded treetop cities of Teldrassil, Auberdine looks outward, serving as the Alliance's busiest port in the north. Regular ships sail between here and the Eastern Kingdoms, to Stormwind Harbor and, by way of Southshore, to Menethil Harbor, while local ferries run to Rut'theran Village at the boughs of the World Tree. Because of its trade role, Auberdine embraces a more cosmopolitan air than traditional elven enclaves; visitors find lamps illuminating stone-laid streets and outland merchants including dwarves and gnomes mingling among the low-slung, arched timber houses. Governed by elder Thundris Windweaver and the Auberdine Village Council, the town coordinates the defence of Darkshore alongside the local Sentinels. Despite its role as a vital trade hub, Auberdine's name is rarely spoken in the boughs of Darnassus, where memory dwells on the great cities the Sundering took. The town endures relentless regional perils: aggressive murlocs raid the fishing boats along the strand, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs press from the south, and foul magic seeping down from Felwood agitates the local wildlife.

subzone:azurelode-mine.text: Azurelode Mine. Azurelode Mine is an active Alliance iron mine nestled in the southwestern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by Southshore's militia and worked by human laborers, its steady supply of ore fuels the local human war effort against the Forsaken of Tarren Mill. Situated southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine has long tapped into the mineral-rich ridges along the coast. Today, human miners labor deep underground under the watchful eye of Foreman Bonds, extracting iron to forge arms and armor for the Alliance defenders holding the region against the Undercity. Because Azurelode Mine supplies the bulk of the raw iron needed to maintain Southshore's garrisons and town militia, it sits directly in the crosshairs of the Horde. Tarren Mill has targeted its workforce and guards in an effort to shatter the supply lines that sustain Hillsbrad's human strongholds.

subzone:ban-ethil-barrow-den.text: Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a sacred subterranean sanctuary hollowed out within the roots of Teldrassil. Originally created as a resting place for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, the cavern complex has recently fallen into chaos. The corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe have overrun its chambers, turning a place of peaceful slumber into a perilous den of madness. Barrow dens serve as sacred resting chambers where night elf druids slumber while projecting their spirits into the Emerald Dream. Ban'ethil Barrow Den was dedicated specifically to sheltering the Druids of the Talon as they communed with nature. Divided into upper and lower subterranean chambers, the den once resonated with tranquil reverie and deep meditative magic. However, the affliction sweeping Teldrassil's wildlife did not spare the Gnarlpine furbolgs, who invaded the complex, turning its hollowed halls into a fortified warren. Driven mad by mysterious corruption taking root across the World Tree, the Gnarlpine tribe drove out or endangered the slumbering druids within Ban'ethil. The furbolgs now fiercely guard the winding tunnels, aggressive toward any night elf who approaches. For the defenders of Teldrassil, reclaiming the barrow den is an urgent priority, not merely to drive back the hostile furbolgs, but to protect the vulnerable druids and sacred relics trapped within its lower depths.

subzone:ban-ethil-hollow.text: Ban'ethil Hollow. Ban'ethil Hollow is a rugged ravine cutting into the woodland just south of the main road connecting Dolanaar and Darnassus. It has become a dangerous haven for corrupted, aggressive furbolgs who pose a constant threat to travelers. Tucked away in the back of the ravine lies the entrance to the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, Ban'ethil Hollow is a sharp reminder that the boughs of Teldrassil are not entirely safe. Furbolgs driven mad by the strange affliction plaguing the World Tree have taken refuge throughout the rocky descent. They frequently stalk the nearby path, waiting to ambush unwary couriers and wandering sentinels. Deep within the ravine sits the threshold of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where slumbering druids and ancient tunnels face encroachment from the maddened beasts outside.

subzone:baradin-bay.text: Baradin Bay. Baradin Bay is the expansive body of water lying between the shores of Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Once vigorously patrolled by the powerful navy of Kul Tiras during the Second War, its waters now conceal treacherous reefs, sunken warships, and hostile aquatic predators. Framed by the coasts of Dun Morogh to the south and Lordaeron to the north, Baradin Bay serves as a vital maritime passage connecting the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. The bay is anchored by busy ports like Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. However, navigating these waters is perilous: shallow sandbanks, jagged shoals, and dangerous fauna like murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks pose constant threats to sailors and travelers alike. During the Second War, Baradin Bay witnessed heavy naval conflict as the fleets of Kul Tiras clashed with the Horde. Today, grim reminders of those battles litter the coast and the seabed. The shattered hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet—known locally as the Lost Fleet—rest half-submerged along the Wetlands coast, while other vessels have plummeted down to Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, opportunistic salvagers, and ravenous sea beasts now haunt the waters surrounding these decaying timber ruins.

subzone:bashal-aran.text: Bashal'Aran. Bashal'Aran is an ancient Highborne ruin situated in northern Darkshore, just east of Auberdine. Once a flourishing sister city to Ameth'Aran before the Great Sundering, the site now crawls with demonic satyrs and grells feeding on lingering arcane magic, while a solitary elven ghost remains trapped by a centuries-old curse. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne subjects in the twin towns of Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran. Governed by the powerful mage Athrikus Narassin, the cities boasted splendid markets and temples dedicated to Elune. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm laid both settlements to waste. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his own second-in-command, the mage Asterion, into a moonstone seal within Bashal'Aran. Even after his physical body perished, Asterion's ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine. In the modern day, the crumbled stones of Bashal'Aran have been claimed by vile squatters: the Deth'ryll satyrs and mischievous grells. Drawn by residual magic clinging to the ancient masonry, these corrupted beings drink in the lingering energy to bolster their foul arts. Though they swarm the broken courtyards and terrorize travelers along Darkshore's forest paths, the demons give a wide berth to the central shrine where Asterion endures his endless vigil.

subzone:bathran-s-haunt.text: Bathran's Haunt. Bathran's Haunt is an ancient kaldorei ruin nestled in northwestern Ashenvale, east of the Zoram Strand. Recently, Forsaken herbalists and their guardians have overtaken the site to harvest local flora for their alchemical research, steadily withering the surrounding woodland. North of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, crumbling night elf pillars stand swallowed by thick Ashenvale foliage. What was once a tranquil kaldorei relic has fallen under the shadow of the Forsaken. Skulking among the broken marble, undead herbalists and their enforcers have set up a crude open-air laboratory. Their presence alone blights the ancient soil: grass rots into a sickly brown, vibrant blossoms wilt, and an unnatural decay creeps through the grove as they methodically harvest rare woodland reagents for their experiments. The primary draw of these ruins is Bathran's Hair, a unique remedial herb found taking root only among these particular stones. While night elf and Alliance scouts view the Forsaken presence as a vile desecration of sacred elven soil, the undead work diligently to extract the plant's potent properties. The Horde maintains a vested interest in the compound's botanical yield, though the Forsaken's secretive methods and the resulting corruption of the earth draw suspicion from outsiders and allies alike.

subzone:beggar-s-haunt.text: Beggar's Haunt. Beggar's Haunt is an abandoned Stormwind scout tower perched on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. While originally built to keep watch over the kingdom's eastern borders, it has become an outpost for Forsaken infiltrators deep within Alliance territory. Perched above the foggy hills east of Manor Mistmantle, Beggar's Haunt was once an active observation post manned by the Stormwind Guard to secure the eastern approaches to the realm. As the region fell into the gloom of modern Duskwood and kingdom patrols withdrew to Darkshire, the stone tower was abandoned to the elements. Today, its commanding vantage point serves a far more sinister purpose: agents of the Forsaken, including members of the Royal Apothecary Society and Deathstalkers, use the ruined stronghold to conduct research and monitor the region under the Alliance's nose. Behind the tower, a steep, twisting path descends to a secluded pool and waterfall known as Knight's Hollow. Here lies an unmarked grave flanked by two ominous hooded stone statues resembling the guardians flanking the Dark Portal. Nearby resting plots, including the burial site of an Unknown Soldier, speak to forgotten clashes fought along this frontier long before the Forsaken moved into the watchtower.

subzone:blackwolf-river.text: Blackwolf River. Blackwolf River is a waterway flowing out of Cragpool Lake down through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Once a clean mountain stream, its waters have become thoroughly polluted by the Venture Company's aggressive logging and industrial operations. Descending from Cragpool Lake, the Blackwolf River cuts across the basin of Windshear Crag. What should be a pristine alpine tributary has instead borne the brunt of unchecked goblin enterprise. As the Venture Company clears the surrounding woodlands with heavy machinery and buzzsaws, sludge, oil, and logging waste leach steadily into the current. The despoiled river stands as a vivid example of the commercial plunder threatening Stonetalon's wilderness.

subzone:blackwood-den.text: Blackwood Den. Blackwood Den is a corrupted furbolg encampment nestled in the southern reaches of Darkshore near the border of Ashenvale. Once a peaceful dwelling, the cave and surrounding camps have fallen into madness alongside the rest of the Blackwood tribe. A lone night elf scout named Volcor sits trapped within the cavern, awaiting aid from Auberdine. Situated near the southern border where Darkshore meets Ashenvale, Blackwood Den consists of a winding network of crude camps and a rocky cave. The Blackwood furbolgs who dwell here have succumbed to the pervasive corruption gripping the region, turning violently hostile toward outsiders. Deep inside the den's cave, the night elf Volcor remains pinned down and endangered by the aggressive tribe, desperately needing assistance from scouts and travelers dispatched from Auberdine.

subzone:bloodtooth-camp.text: Bloodtooth Camp. Bloodtooth Camp is an encampment of hostile, corrupted furbolgs tucked into central Ashenvale, situated just west of the Falfarren River. Led by the chieftain Ran Bloodtooth, these once-peaceful creatures have succumbed to dark madness and attack anyone who approaches. The camp is a primary target for Alliance scouts working to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Nestled southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River, Bloodtooth Camp serves as a stark reminder of Ashenvale's encroaching decay. The furbolgs living here were once connected to the sacred wilderness of Kalimdor, but a lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Under the command of Ran Bloodtooth, they guard their crude settlement with rabid hostility, turning upon travelers and night elven protectors alike.

subzone:bough-shadow.text: Bough Shadow. Bough Shadow is a secluded grove tucked away in the far northeastern corner of Ashenvale, east of Forest Song. It centers around a colossal Great Tree rooted over an ancient portal leading directly into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow houses one of the rare Great Trees, its roots plunging deep into the earth around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. Today, the tranquil yet imposing grove is heavily guarded by the Green Dragonflight. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while patrols of Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles keep a vigilant, unyielding watch over the swirling green portal at its base, turning away any mortal who approaches unbidden.

subzone:boulderslide-cavern.text: Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide Cavern is a subterranean warren tucked at the deepest end of Boulderslide Ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as the primary den and excavation site for the local Boulderslide kobolds, who obsessively tunnel in search of glowing mineral formations. The Boulderslide kobolds have burrowed deep into the crags of Stonetalon, establishing Boulderslide Cavern as their stronghold. Unlike ordinary vermin merely seeking shelter, these kobolds mine frantically for resonite, a rare glowing purple crystal embedded throughout the stone. The crystals pulse with lingering earthen magic, driving the creatures into a defensive frenzy against any intruders who approach their dig.

subzone:boulderslide-ravine.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network. Opposite the entrance to Boulderslide Cavern lies a small, quiet cave overlooking the ravine. Lit by rough torches and stacked with weathered supply barrels, the shelter contains primitive tribal paintings across its interior walls. The crude artwork bears a striking resemblance to ancient tauren designs, suggesting that native tribes traveled or sought temporary shelter in these crags long before modern conflict swept into the mountains.

subzone:brackwell-pumpkin-patch.text: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Brackwell Pumpkin Patch is an overrun farmstead in southeastern Elwynn Forest. Once home to the Brackwell family, the fields and cottage have been thoroughly seized by the Defias Brotherhood as an operational hideout. It serves as a meeting point for rogue conspirators and a staging ground for smuggling stolen gold. Situated southeast of the Stonefield homestead, the Brackwell farm was once a productive patch of Elwynn farmland. Today, the rightful owners have vanished without a trace, driven out or worse by the rising criminal tide. In their absence, the Defias Brotherhood claimed the farm's sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. The area functions as a safehouse and transfer post, where brigands regroup away from the watchful eyes of Goldshire's patrols. High-profile conspirators like Morgan the Collector use the isolated patch to receive shipments of illicitly gathered gold skimmed from the forest's mines.

subzone:brewnall-village.text: Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village is a small dwarven settlement nestled in Chill Breeze Valley near the entrance to Gnomeregan. Established by the Barleybrew family, this outpost serves as a proving ground for bold brewing experiments and regional defense against wild beasts. Despite being called a village, it functions largely as a rustic encampment in the snowy gnomish lowlands of Dun Morogh. Tucked away in the snowdrifts of Chill Breeze Valley, Brewnall Village lies squarely within the traditional gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The settlement is home to the Barleybrew clan, stalwart dwarven brewers devoted to perfecting age-old recipes and crafting the ultimate stout. Though dubbed a village, the outpost consists mostly of tents and outdoor brewing equipment rather than permanent stone architecture. Between testing experimental batches of ale and defending against the ferocious local wolves and bears, the Barleybrews rely heavily on wandering mountaineers to gather rare ingredients and keep the valley secure.

subzone:brightwood-grove.text: Brightwood Grove. Brightwood Grove is a shadowed expanse of woodland located just west of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once part of the region's serene agrarian landscape, it is now infested with savage Nightbane worgen who make camp among ruined homesteads and attack any travelers wandering too close. Situated within sight of Darkshire's perimeter, Brightwood Grove represents the creeping peril threatening the town's borders. The homesteads and fences that once demarcated peaceful farmland now lie collapsed and rotting. In their place, crude camps have been erected by the Nightbane worgen, who prowl the overgrown clearings. The proximity of these wolf-beasts poses an ongoing threat to the town, forcing the Night Watch and passing adventurers to continually cull their numbers before the settlement is overrun.

subzone:calmbreeze-inn.text: Calmbreeze Inn. Calmbreeze Inn refers to the primary establishments offering shelter and services across Zephras Isle, found in both Shen'dar Village and Valaanar. They serve as essential rest stops for travelers exploring the island, housing local trade trainers, innkeepers, and historical artifacts. The Calmbreeze Inns provide sanctuary amid the winding trails of Zephras Isle. In Shen'dar Village, the inn operates under Coriella Calmbreeze and doubles as a central hub where island tradesfolk gather, including mentors in herbalism, skinning, and enchanting. Across the way in Valaanar, another Calmbreeze Inn accommodates local wayfarers and shelters rare curios, including an audio crystal recording the history of the ancient rebellion in Eldre'Thalas.

subzone:camp-aparaje.text: Camp Aparaje. Camp Aparaje was once a peaceful tauren village nestled in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Today, it lies overrun and occupied by the hostile Grimtotem tribe, who slaughtered the original settlers and took the outpost for themselves. Perched along the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, Camp Aparaje was established by peaceful tauren looking to live quietly in the highlands. That tranquility was shattered when raiders from the nearby Grimtotem Post, led by Grundig Darkcloud, launched a brutal and unprovoked assault. The villagers were butchered or driven away, and survivors such as Makaba Flathoof were left mourning the destruction of their home while dreading the fate of captive kin. Now completely occupied by Grimtotem warriors, Camp Aparaje serves as a forward base of operations for the aggressive tribe in the region. Unlike typical Grimtotem settlements that fly blue markings, the great totem standing in Aparaje is carved with deep crimson paint.

subzone:canals-stormwind-city.text: Canals (Stormwind City). The Canals are a network of stone-lined waterways weaving through Stormwind City, separating its distinct districts. They serve as quiet thoroughfares for pedestrians and anglers, while quietly harboring hidden hazards and the entrance to the city's prison. The Canals link and define the districts of Stormwind, dividing the bustling markets of the Trade District from the aged alleys of Old Town, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges, archways, and waterside walkways frame quiet establishments like the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet residential homes. In addition to serving local merchants and recreational fishermen, the waterways conceal the fortified entrance to the Stockade, where Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels are held beneath street level. The placid surface of the waterways belies a violent past. When the Horde sacked Stormwind during the First War, the city was left in ruins, and the canals were restored only as the capital was rebuilt after the Second War. Today, while cleaned and restored, the depths retain an air of mystery, fueled by city rumors of a massive albino crocolisk prowling beneath the docks.

subzone:cathedral-of-light.text: Cathedral of Light. The Cathedral of Light is the spiritual heart of Stormwind City and the primary sanctuary of the Church of the Holy Light. Standing tall over Cathedral Square, it serves as the central bastion for human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Rebuilt after its devastation during the First War under the guidance of Archbishop Alonsus Faol and then-Bishop Benedictus, the Cathedral of Light stands as a towering beacon of resilience. With the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge during the Third War, the seat of the Church shifted south to Stormwind. Today, Archbishop Benedictus shepherds the faithful from this grand hall, providing spiritual guidance to the entire Alliance. Beyond serving as a house of prayer and healing, the cathedral acts as the primary headquarters for the remaining Knights of the Silver Hand in the southern kingdoms. High-ranking figures such as Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker and Duthorian Rall train promising squires through the sacred trials of the Tome of Valor and the Tome of Divinity. Alongside them, High Priestess Laurena guides devout acolytes in the deepest tenets of the Light, preparing holy champions to defend the realm against the rising threat of the Defias Brotherhood and the Scourge.

subzone:cathedral-square.text: Cathedral Square. Cathedral Square is the spiritual and civic heart of Stormwind City, dominated by the majestic Cathedral of Light. Beyond serving as a place of worship and devotion, the bustling plaza houses municipal institutions like City Hall, the city orphanage, and the regional headquarters of the Argent Dawn. Situated northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square serves as the epicenter of faith in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Dominating the skyline is the Cathedral of Light, the preeminent sanctuary for followers of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers gather here to study, pray, and train. Citizens, pilgrims, and local schoolchildren led by School Mistress Danna regularly mingle in the square for conversation and contemplation. The district is not merely reserved for prayer; it is one of the capital's busiest civic centers. The square houses the Stormwind Orphanage as well as City Hall, anchoring the administrative life of the kingdom. Specialized armorers and weaponsmiths catering to holy crusaders, such as Righteous Plates and Just Maces, line the avenues. It also serves as the base of operations for the Argent Dawn within Stormwind, where recruiters and representatives coordinate relief efforts and rally champions against the encroaching threats of the Scourge in the northern kingdoms.

subzone:cenarion-enclave.text: Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Enclave is the verdant northwestern district of Darnassus, serving as the central gathering place and seat of power for the Cenarion Circle in the capital. While Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage lies slumbering within the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the night elven druids from the great hollows and living boughs of this grove. Occupying a high terrace above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave is shaped from ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Convocations of the Cenarion Circle gather within structures molded directly from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here, pushing his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite lingering political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Beyond the druids who meditate among its streams, the enclave also hosts the capital's elven hunters and the stables where skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers. Though renowned as a tranquil sanctuary of nature, the enclave harbors more covert activities. Beneath the hollowed roots of the westernmost bough lies a subterranean refuge used by Darnassus's clandestine rogues, who conduct their quiet business shielded by the rustling canopy above.

subzone:champions-hall.text: Champions' Hall. Tucked away in the southern reaches of Old Town, the Champions' Hall serves as the officer's barracks and supply armory for the Alliance's decorated veterans in Stormwind. Beyond its threshold, quartermasters dispense specialized weapons, plate, and regalia to proven warriors of the faction. Access is strictly guarded, reserved only for officers who have demonstrated valor on the field of war. Hidden behind a guarded threshold in Old Town, the Champions' Hall is a restricted haven for the Alliance's most distinguished combatants. Military commanders gather here over tactical maps of Azeroth to confer on ongoing campaigns, flanked by armaments and the grand insignias of rank. Only soldiers who have climbed the Alliance hierarchy to achieve officer status—specifically the rank of Knight or higher—are permitted entry. Inside, military quartermasters supply battle-hardened soldiers with elite arms, armor, and mounts crafted specifically to turn the tide against the Horde in contested zones across the world.

subzone:charred-vale.text: Charred Vale. The Charred Vale is a smoldering valley in southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, devastated by the reckless deforestation and machinery of the Venture Company. Once a thriving haven for treants and chimaeras, it is now engulfed in flames, roving elementals, and hostile harpies. Not long ago, this southwest basin was a flourishing alpine wood guarded by majestic treants and inhabited by native chimaeras and harpies. Its ruin began with the arrival of the Venture Company. The greedy goblin outfit clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the guardians and awakening chaotic fire elementals. Though the treants eventually forced the goblins back, the land was left broken, scarred by fire, and tainted by whatever foul devices the retreating loggers deployed. Today, blackened ancients wander blindly through smoke and ash alongside enraged elementals. Bloodfury harpies roost in the skeletal snags, defending what remains of their territory. Despite the hostility of the valley, druids from Sun Rock Retreat refuse to abandon the region, dispatching travelers to sow enchanted seeds and tend the corrupted ancients in a persistent campaign to reclaim the scorched earth.

subzone:chill-breeze-valley.text: Chill Breeze Valley. Chill Breeze Valley is a rugged, snow-covered pass in western Dun Morogh linking the dwarven settlement of Kharanos with the embattled city of Gnomeregan. While its main path is a well-traveled thoroughfare for young travelers and refugees, its secluded recesses harbor dangerous beasts and bloody dens. Chill Breeze Valley forms a T-shaped trench through the mountains of western Dun Morogh. The main east-west trail sees steady foot traffic from novice dwarves and gnomes journeying between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. However, straying into the valley's north-south offshoot is another matter entirely. Strewn with bloodstains and mangled carcasses, these shadowy reaches harbor ferocious predators—most notably savage wendigos that lair in deep ice caves and prey on anyone reckless enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

subzone:clean-zone.text: Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery. Beyond serving as a military redoubt, the Clean Zone is a hub for salvaging the lost capital. Gnomish engineers installed Sparklematic 5200 units to chemically scrub and wash grime-encrusted relics hauled out of the city's radioactive underbelly. Technicians and merchants like Tink Sprocketwhistle process these reclaimed gears and baubles, outfitting adventurers while studying the lingering toxic fallout that plagues the deep tunnels.

subzone:cleft.text: Cleft. The Cleft is a darkened hollow located northwest of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil corner of the boughs, it has been claimed by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, who use it as a stronghold to ambush travelers moving along the main highway toward Darnassus. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, the Cleft has turned into one of the most perilous dens on the world tree. Driven mad by the foul taint spreading through Teldrassil, the resident Gnarlpine furbolgs have fortified this hollow. From this redoubt, the maddened beasts terrorize the local roads, threatening to cut Dolanaar off from the capital.

subzone:cliffspring-falls.text: Cliffspring Falls. Cliffspring Falls marks the dramatic origin of Darkshore's vital Cliffspring River, tumbling down from the eastern cliffs into the coastal forest. Long celebrated as the principal source of clean drinking water for the region, its waters have recently fallen victim to a foul, spreading taint. The subterranean cavern feeding the waterfall has become infested with hostile naga and shadowy Twilight's Hammer cultists. Pouring out from caverns perched high in the rocky bluffs along Darkshore's eastern border, Cliffspring Falls feeds the Cliffspring River, which winds westward across the woods to empty into the sea. Traditionally, this cascade provided the purest drinking water for local night elf settlements. In recent times, however, the waters have turned foul and murky, spreading sickness and ecological decay throughout the river basin. Investigating naturalists have discovered that the cave network at the falls' headwaters is overrun by vile naga and dark cultists, who plot in the shadows while demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

subzone:coldridge-pass.text: Coldridge Pass. Coldridge Pass is a rugged, snowbound tunnel cutting through the southern mountain ridge of Dun Morogh. It serves as the sole overland route connecting the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley to the rest of the kingdom, emerging near the bustling town of Kharanos. Because hostile troggs have overrun the passage, any traveler attempting the journey must either fight their way through or make a desperate dash for the other side. For young dwarven recruits and gnome novices taking their first steps beyond Coldridge Valley, Coldridge Pass is a harsh rite of passage. Chiseled straight through the rock, this tunnel forms the primary link sending newly trained adventurers eastward toward the frontier hub of Kharanos. What was once a secure mountain corridor has become a perilous choke point, infested with aggressive troggs that have pushed up from dark sub-terrains to menace any soul trying to travel between the sheltered valley and the wider reaches of Dun Morogh.

subzone:command-center.text: Command Center. The Command Center, often referred to as the Stormwind Barracks, stands in the heart of Old Town as the operational headquarters for the city's military officers. In peacetime, it houses the standing army, but with Stormwind's forces dispatched to distant frontiers, it currently operates with a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. Situated within the weathered streets of Old Town, the Command Center serves as the primary garrison and martial training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind. Normally packed with regular infantry and ranking officers, the facility is uncharacteristically sparse. With much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad, the barracks relies on a veteran cadre of instructors—including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen—to train fresh warriors to bolster the city's defenses. Guards throughout Stormwind often direct newcomers to the 'Barracks' when seeking instruction in heavy arms and tactical combat. The building's proximity to both the Pig and Whistle Tavern and the shadowy operations elsewhere in Old Town makes it an essential anchor of order in a district known for tavern brawls and roguish activity.

subzone:commons.text: Commons. The Commons serves as the vibrant commercial heart of Ironforge, connecting the city entrance directly to its vast caverns. Teeming with merchants, travelers, and bankers, it is the busiest thoroughfare in the dwarven capital and the central marketplace for the entire Alliance. Located just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge, the Commons is the first district that greets travelers entering the mountain kingdom. Carved directly out of the stone, this bustling market street houses the primary Alliance Auction House, the Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank within the Vault of Ironforge. Broad avenues connect it seamlessly to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward, ensuring that nearly all foot traffic in the mountain passes through its bustling storefronts. Due to Ironforge's central location on the Eastern Kingdoms continent and its direct underground Deeprun Tram link to Stormwind, the Commons functions as the Alliance's primary trade nexus. Adventurers converge here to trade goods brought from every corner of Azeroth, purchase armaments from Steelfury's Weapon Emporium and reagents from Barim, or meet under the warm lantern light of the local inn before heading out into the Khaz Modan snows.

subzone:craftsmen-s-terrace.text: Craftsmen's Terrace. The Craftsmen's Terrace is the bustling artisan district situated in the northern reaches of Darnassus. It serves as the primary trade and manufacturing hub for the night elf capital, housing workshops, profession trainers, and a lively inn. The district also hosts external representatives, including an embassy for the neutral Argent Dawn. Spanning the northern edge of the canopy city, the Craftsmen's Terrace gathers the diverse trades that keep Darnassus running. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans operate their shops here, integrating classic night elven methods with practical craft. The district also provides essential community amenities, including an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors. Bridges connect the terrace directly to the Cenarion Enclave to the west and the Warrior's Terrace to the south. Despite the kaldorei's historic isolation, the Craftsmen's Terrace is home to foreign connections, most notably an embassy established by the Argent Dawn to coordinate with northern allies against the Scourge. Visitors browsing the district's various workshops might also stumble across scattered scholarly volumes, ranging from historical accounts of the War of the Ancients to chronicles detailing the Second War and esoteric treatises on the Old Gods.

subzone:cragpool-lake.text: Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company.
